text:
nina: heads-up — since ~03:20 UTC ap-southeast1 is showing a sharp drop in ephemeral NVMe IOPS on the gpu pool. GPU attaches are piling up and some jobs are timing out.
kevin: how sharp? numbers?
nina: attach backlog up to ~210 (normal ~12). attach latency jumped from ~120ms -> ~3s. scrub backlog doubled on affected hosts.
samir: any dmesg / SMART showing errors? can you paste one node log?
nina: sharing snippet from node gnode-aps1-042 (trimmed):
```
[ 4078.345678] nvme0: I/O 0 QID 3 timeout, rqd 0
[ 4078.345689] nvme0: read timeout, retrying
[ 4078.345701] nvme0: media error, lba 0x1f2a3b4
[ 4079.000000] scrub: backlog 214 -> 498
```
kevin: looks like transient read retries + scrub chasing hot blocks. any firmware churn recently?
nina: no firmware push in the last 7 days for that cohort. cloud metrics show a correlated small net-IO spike at 03:18 UTC then the tail.
beth (oncall): tagging @janitor-bot to pause non-critical deep scrubs in the region for 1h to buy us headroom. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
janitor-bot: pausing deep-scrub jobs with tag region:ap-southeast1 for 1h (triggered by beth).
nina: confirming pausing scrub reduced write amplification but attach backlog still drifting.
samir: mitigation plan: 1) pause deep scrubs (done), 2) temporarily drain GPU scheduling to healthiest AZ, 3) mark worst 8 nodes as unsched until disk health investigated, 4) schedule controlled firmware probe for a small cohort. thoughts?
kevin: +1. also consider throttling background GC on scrub process and move heavy batch jobs to eu-west2 for next 2h.
beth (oncall): I'll open INC ticket and route to storage team. https://redwood.internal/INC-4921
kevin: run `sudo nvme get-log /dev/nvme0 --log-id=2` on a bad host and paste output to the ticket.
nina: running now, will paste to INC-4921. quick grep of node fleet shows ~12% of nodes expose media errors, concentrated in 2 racks.
samir: that clustering suggests a shared power or cooling transient or a firmware cohort. can we correlate host firmware versions?
nina: initial look: 6 of the bad nodes share firmware v2.8.1, others are mixed.
beth (oncall): ops-sre, please notify capacity team — expect ~10-15% temporary capacity hit while we cordon nodes.
kevin: if we cordon those nodes, we should flip autoscaler to prefer dedicated capacity for any critical customers in ap-southeast1 to avoid SLA hits.
samir: also add a temporary routing rule: GPU attaches with >3s latency fall back to eu-west2 for best-effort jobs.
nina: doing a small cordon now on the 8 worst nodes and moving pending attaches off them. will report impact in 10m.
janitor-bot: cordon applied to gnode-aps1-042, gnode-aps1-047, gnode-aps1-081, gnode-aps1-089, gnode-aps1-094, gnode-aps1-101, gnode-aps1-122, gnode-aps1-130.
kevin: thanks. can we capture io_latency histograms and share in the ticket? want pre/post scrub-pause plots.
nina: uploading metrics to INC-4921 now. pre-pause p95 token latency for attach: 3.1s, post-pause (5m) down to 1.4s. backlog down from 210 -> 86.
beth (oncall): good progress. next steps: storage team to run nvme diag on the firmware cohort, ops-sre to validate rack cooling/pdu logs, and capacity to announce temporary scheduling constraints to customers. I'll keep alerting quieted and update status.
samir: if firmware probe confirms a problematic series, plan a staged firmware rollout with canary and rollback. avoid sweeping updates during peak hours.
kevin: note on cost: moving batch jobs to eu-west2 will increase egress/cross-region cost; track that under INC-4921 for billing.
nina: FYI some nodes show elevated SMART Media_Error_Count — collecting full SMART dumps into the ticket.
beth (oncall): Nice triage team. keep chat updates short; if we need hands-on, we'll spin up a call. :phone:
kevin: one last ask — add a short eval prompt to Redwood Optimize to track model cold-start sensitivity to attach latency; might help detect future regressions earlier.
samir: agree. adding a TODO in INC-4921.
janitor-bot: scrub pause auto-resumes at 1h from 03:27 UTC unless extended manually.
nina: updating INC-4921 with the diag outputs and current backlog. will report back in 15m with attach backlog trend.
beth (oncall): thanks all. good catch and quick mitigation. :thumbsup:
